summary: Idaho's sitting governor, Brad Little (Republican), ran again and won a third term, defeating Terri Pickens (Democrat).

candidates.name: Brad Little
candidates.bio: Brad Little is a Republican who has served as governor of Idaho since January 2019. A third-generation rancher from Emmett, he was appointed to the Idaho Senate in 2001, then served as lieutenant governor from 2009 to 2019.

positions.summary: Says he has delivered historic tax relief while keeping the budget balanced and without raising taxes.
Points to Operation No Return, which his campaign describes as removing dangerous criminals who are in the country illegally from Idaho communities.
Says he has delivered historic teacher pay raises, a fivefold boost in literacy funding and expanded school choice.
His campaign lists promoting pro-life policies among the values he defends.

candidates.name: Terri Pickens
candidates.bio: Terri Pickens is a Democrat who won her party's primary for governor in May 2026 with about 61% of the vote. She was the Democratic nominee for lieutenant governor in 2022 and has been described in local news as a Boise attorney. Her campaign says she is not a career politician.

positions.summary: Says she would support small businesses, maintain a stable tax structure, ensure a living wage and strengthen unions and worker protections.
Says health care must be affordable and accessible to all Idahoans.
Says people who enter illegally should be treated humanely, violent criminals deported, and simple pathways created for immigrant workers.
Says she would repeal the school voucher program and increase funding for teacher salaries, pre-K and rural schools.
Says women have a fundamental right to bodily autonomy and that family planning decisions belong to women, not the government.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (MultiState governors tracker, updated Nov 4, 35 of 36 races called). Summary note moved: AP projected the win; final vote shares were not confirmed.
